"Risom et al., 2018" refers specifically to a 2018 qualitative interview study by Risom and colleagues that explores patients' experiences with individual education regarding atrial fibrillation (AF) [^src1]. This article disambiguates this specific publication from other studies conducted by the same author [^src1].

The study is highly significant for providing the patient perspective on the importance of individualized education in AF care [^src1]. It reveals that patients consider individual education crucial for living a good life with the disease [^src1]. Interviews showed that patients needed a healthcare professional, such as a nurse, to talk to in order to overcome their fear of death and regain confidence in their physical capacity and strength [^src1]. Ultimately, the education provided patients with the practical tools necessary to manage both their physical symptoms and their anxiety [^src1].

Within the broader narrative of the AFDK 2025 annual report, this publication serves as a foundational piece of evidence for [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]], which measures patient education as a quality indicator [^src1]. By defining the patient perspective, Risom et al. (2018) bridges international evidence and national clinical guidelines with the lived, human dimension of quality measurement in cardiology [^src1].

## Mentions

- Page 84: "Patienterne beskriver deres erfaringer med individuel undervisning om AF som værende afgørende for at leve et godt liv med sygdom. I et studie er patienter blevet interviewet og her fortæller de at havde brug for en sundhedsprofessionel (her sygeplejerske) at tale med for at komme over dødsangst samt genvinde troen på egen fysiske kapacitet og styrke. Patienterne fik gennem undervisningen redskaber til at håndtere symptomer og angst (Risom et al., 2018)." [^src1]
